correctness.rationale: For equilibrium observation the age density is Pr(T>l)/E[T], including a uniform age for deterministic T. The binomially attenuated |2> populations give m1=A/μ and m2=B/(2μ). Substitution into the first three number-state Wigner polynomials gives P(u)=1+((8u−4)A+(4u²−8u+2)B)/μ. Since A<B<2A, its vertex is u=1−A/B in (0,1/2); the minimum is 1−Φ/μ. P(0)=E[(1−2exp(−γL))²]>0 by the continuous age law, so a strict negative minimum gives precisely a nonempty annulus (and the endpoint formula follows by solving the square). The Hessian of Φ is the positive rank-one form (8/B)(1,−A/B)⊗(1,−A/B). For a deterministic wait t, Φ=2 tanh(t/2)(1+exp(−2t)); differentiating with z=exp(−t) gives the stated negative second derivative, since the numerator polynomial is 2z⁴+5z³+3(z−1/2)²+1/4. Two Jensen steps are finite (A,B bounded and Φ is bounded on the physical cone); the second is strict for every nonconstant wait. Thus the exact witness and the claimed equality cases follow, and φ(t)/t strictly falls from 2 to 0, proving the unique positive crossing and the double zero only for the deterministic clock at threshold. Independent 72-digit decimal bisection of 2(1−exp(−t))(1+exp(−2t))/(1+exp(−t))−t on [0.5,2] gives 1.13035954884518811444…, not the last digits in the frozen Finding. At mean 0.9 independent substitution gives minima −0.09252987058 and +0.12544519193. Supplied files were inspected, not executed; finite tests are not the proof. The claim is about sign feasibility, not integrated negativity, full-Wigner ordering, or nonrenewal clocks.
